findings.finding: REGION decoder accepts values beyond its declared step, sample and region limits; duplicate seq and non-finite seq are also accepted. Host line length is bounded, so this does not establish unbounded allocation or actual bad device replies.

Both validateProfile and resolveDeviceProfile return a typed profile accepting non-string calibration values and non-numeric control coordinates. HID serialization has later finitePoint checks; this does not prove unsafe touches pass all execution gates.

Cast gate exemption is syntax based: a closing return value as unknown as T is excluded even without guards. Library JSON.parse any propagation also escapes the explicit any and annotated parse counters. Strict compilation can pass a program that crashes on the asserted type.

counterProbes.input: function unchecked(value: unknown): number { return value as unknown as number; }

findings.finding: validateArtifactRef accepts NaN size; validateManifest accepts an array for artifacts although it returns Record<string,unknown>. V1 contracts intentionally leave other fields unknown; that documented openness is distinct from these checked-field gaps.

Companion host contract tests compile and pass, but exclude Java sources importing Android (16/35 source files). Current CI has no Android APK build step discovered by searching its workflows. Device state, installed APK identity, Android runtime behavior and resource budgets remain unmeasured here.
Ratchets pass with debt: 1659 unchecked casts, 1733 strict Python errors and 104 deep imports. Zero explicit any and non-null assertions is achieved, but does not make boundary validation complete.

54 contract rows have fixture links, but catalog presence proves neither rejection coverage nor validator completeness. artifact-ref-v1 and claim-evidence-v1 point at the evidence CLI source as conformance fixtures. CONTRACTS omits claim-envelope-v1, while register contains it; no equality gate was found.
